content.comment_body: Hello, I'm wondering if anyone knows a way to monitor the output current of a device output. For instance, I plan to connect an actuator to a [company_name] [product_name] relay output and want to check the actuator's current to determine if it is blocked or under strain. My initial idea was to use a current transducer that converts current to a 0-10V signal, but I haven't found a suitable one. Is there another method to achieve this? Thanks, [user_name]
Hello, You can monitor the current with a multimeter, but you need to place the multimeter in series with the circuit.

Hi [user_name], Thank you for your response. My goal is to manage the actuator automatically. When the output current exceeds, for example, 3 amps (detected through an analog input), I want the system to stop the output, serving as protection against high current for the actuator. I'll look into DC current to DC voltage converters. Thanks, [user_name]
[url] I think you need a current transducer without a current transformer; 5 amps rating is suitable for actuators.

A straightforward solution is a current monitoring relay, which generates a digital signal if current goes beyond a defined threshold. These are widely available for DC, single-phase, or 3-phase actuators from many popular brands. If you want an analog signal from the current, use a sensor like a shunt resistor or a current transformer along with an instrument amplifier. This is easy to implement in electronics, but harder to source as ready-made control hardware. Some motor drives can be programmed to provide suitable analog or digital outputs as well. [user_name]
Thanks everyone for your responses. I'll research current monitoring relays and share any findings here on the forum. I've found a product that may work for my needs: [url] Thanks again, [user_name]
